articles.title: Home Assistant tackles background crashes on iPhone and Apple Watch
articles.dek: Saved home views and phone shortcuts wait for the app to open, while watch updates run one at a time.
body: Home Assistant changes background work linked to crashes in its iPhone and Apple Watch apps. Contributor Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves associates the watch’s saved-home loading with reports from roughly 2,000 devices on version 2026.9.3, and the phone’s shortcut refresh with reports from about 876 devices.

Loading the watch’s saved home view and rebuilding iPhone home-screen shortcuts wait until the app is active. That avoids background database reads which the operating system could interrupt while leaving a lock held.

The watch also applies incoming home updates one at a time. Overlapping updates could exceed its processing allowance; it refreshes the display after the last update in a burst instead of after each one.

pullRequests.title: Defer app icon shortcut refresh to the foreground
Defer the watch home cache load to the foreground
Apply pushed watch mirrors one at a time

articles.title: Music Assistant adapts fades to mixed-tempo playlists
articles.dek: Quiet intros and outros overlap, while filters and echoes keep incompatible drum beats apart.
body: Music Assistant expands Smart Fades beyond tracks that can share a beat. Songs with different tempos or time signatures can overlap through their quiet intros and outros for up to 15 seconds, instead of routinely receiving a short cut.

Marcel van der Veldt adds filter and echo transitions for pairs whose drum beats would clash, and avoids changing the tempo when there is no beat to match. Existing beatmatched transitions remain, with checks against overlapping vocals and drums.
In van der Veldt’s replay of 3,000 random pairs drawn from 1,500 analysed tracks, the median planned fade grew from 3.9 to 7.7 seconds. The measurement compares transition plans for that collection.

pullRequests.title: Smart fades: longer, smoother transitions between tracks that can't be beatmatched
Smart fades: only stretch the tempo where both tracks have a beat
Smart fades: filter out and echo out when two beats don't match

articles.title: Music Assistant lets its AI DJ talk over a song’s intro
articles.dek: An optional segment setting lowers the music beneath the voice and ends the talk-over before singing starts.
body: Music Assistant adds an optional Talk over the intro setting to AI Radio segments. The end of the host’s spoken break can play over the start of the next song, with the music lowered beneath the voice and the overlap ending before the first sung line.

The timing follows the version of the song that actually plays, using its audio analysis or synchronized lyrics. If there is no usable timing, or the intro or spoken break is too short, the whole break plays separately as before.
Marcel van der Veldt supplies the server work, alongside jpittelkow’s first contribution to the frontend. The setting starts off and is chosen separately for each segment.

Time the AI DJ's talk-over to the version of the song that actually plays
Let a DJ segment talk over the intro of the next song
Document the AI Radio "Talk over the intro" option
Let a stream declare a tail overlap over the next queue item
Label the voice-over transition in the audio processing details

articles.title: Music Assistant cuts the wait when adding to large queues
articles.dek: Smart Fades ordering works in small batches instead of reordering thousands of tracks at once.
body: Music Assistant avoids a long stall when adding music to a large shuffled queue with Optimize order for Smart Fades enabled. Instead of comparing every waiting track at once, it orders the next 25 and prepares later batches while music plays.

In Marcel van der Veldt’s test with a 6,500-track queue, adding 40 tracks fell from 23 seconds to 0.04 seconds. Tracks stay within their batches, so music with existing analysis no longer jumps ahead of unfamiliar tracks, and the queue keeps following the song that is actually playing.

pullRequests.title: Adding music to a large shuffled queue no longer takes a minute

articles.title: ESPHome brings direct device messaging to ESP8266 boards
articles.dek: Makers can exchange sensor readings directly between devices using a chip family previously left out.
body: ESPHome adds ESP-NOW support to ESP8266 boards, letting makers use the existing direct wireless messaging actions and sensor transport on that chip family. The same component previously supported ESP32 only.

Mathew Winstone supplies the addition in his first contribution to ESPHome. ESP8266 messages remain limited to the older protocol’s smaller payload size, and it cannot distinguish broadcast packets from other received packets. J. Nick Koston reviewed the work.

pullRequests.title: [espnow] Add support for ESPNow with ESP8266

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps MELCloud devices through empty cloud replies
articles.dek: An empty reply stops erasing the devices and the customizations attached to them.
body: Home Assistant keeps MELCloud Home devices when the cloud service unexpectedly returns an empty account. Previously, one such reply removed every device and its entity customizations. The devices instead become unavailable until the service reports them again.
Erwin Douna preserves their last known details while they are unavailable. If an owner really removes every unit from the account, the retained unavailable devices need to be removed manually.

pullRequests.title: Keep MELCloud Home devices when the account returns no units

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps your library intact when a share disconnects
articles.dek: A missing drive under a Local files folder stops looking like deleted music, including after a restart.
body: Music Assistant preserves tracks when a drive or share beneath a Local files source is temporarily unavailable. A source reading a parent folder such as /media previously treated an offline share as empty and removed its tracks, recreating them when the share returned.

Marcel van der Veldt also covers Home Assistant shares that are already offline when the server starts. If Home Assistant’s share list cannot be read, that synchronization avoids deletions. Removing a storage location permanently still lets its tracks leave the library; cloud and WebDAV sources are unchanged.

pullRequests.title: Keep tracks of a disconnected share when syncing the folder above it
Keep the tracks of a share that was already down when the server started

articles.title: Music Assistant restores MSX television queues and changes grouping
articles.dek: The updated connection also retires its own grouping and browser player, with Universal Groups as the replacement.
body: Music Assistant corrects MSX Bridge playback on televisions and consoles that manage their own playlist, including Samsung Tizen and Xbox. These devices could stop after the first song because later track requests failed authentication. The revised connection follows Music Assistant’s queue directly.

The provider update restores repeat controls, choosing queue items and continuing at the end through Endless Mix. It removes its own TV grouping, Shared Buffer mode, browser player and Sendspin bridge client. Owners should use Universal Groups for grouping; an upgrade removes the retired settings and old bridge-created Sendspin players, and switches Shared Buffer setups to Independent delivery.

pullRequests.title: Update MSX Bridge provider from v1.4.9 to v1.6.2
Fix MSX Bridge TVs going silent after the first track

articles.title: Home Assistant stops failed actions from appearing successful
articles.dek: Twenty integrations report errors back to the automation instead of only writing them to a log.
body: Home Assistant changes action handling in 20 integrations so a failed command no longer looks successful while the automation carries on. Errors reach the caller with a translated explanation, including failures in Discord notifications, Neato controls and Yamaha actions.

Erwin Douna distinguishes a rejected command from invalid input, such as an unsupported fan speed or scene. Notifications sent to several recipients still try each recipient before reporting any failure.

pullRequests.title: Raise errors instead of logging in action handlers

articles.title: Piper brings speaker and speech-speed choices to its web page
articles.dek: The local speech server’s page exposes voice settings that previously required a separate API request.
body: Piper’s web page gains controls for choosing a speaker and changing how speech is generated, including speaking rate. People evaluating a local voice can try its alternatives without leaving the browser to write an API request.

Michael Hansen adds sliders and number fields, a speaker selector for voices that contain several speakers, and a reset to the voice’s defaults. Chosen settings survive each new speech sample. The controls are in Piper’s own web server.

pullRequests.title: Choose a speaker and the synthesis scales from the web page

articles.title: Music Assistant completes Home Assistant sign-ins away from home
articles.dek: Web and mobile sign-ins return to the public address instead of an unreachable home-network address.
body: Music Assistant fixes Sign in with Home Assistant when the web or mobile app is opened through an External URL or Remote Access. The return journey uses the public address rather than sending the browser to an internal address it cannot reach. The mobile correction works with existing app versions.
This route requires a Music Assistant External URL. Without one, the Remote Access interface hides the Home Assistant sign-in button because the return journey cannot complete.

pullRequests.title: Fix Home Assistant sign-in through the External URL or Remote Access
Fix Home Assistant sign-in from the mobile app through the External URL or Remote Access
Hide Home Assistant sign-in on Remote Access without an External URL

articles.title: ESPHome gives electricity-meter readings their correct units
articles.dek: Teleinfo measurements stop defaulting to energy counters; existing setups may need a statistics repair.
body: ESPHome automatically assigns the right units and measurement types to known Teleinfo electricity-meter readings. Current, voltage and apparent-power readings no longer inherit the same watt-hour energy-counter defaults as accumulated consumption.

Frédéric Metrich supplies matching configuration guidance. Existing Home Assistant statistics may ask for a repair when a sensor’s unit changes. To retain an older definition for a known tag, the owner must explicitly set both its unit and device class; unknown tags keep their previous defaults.

[teleinfo] Document pre-defined sensor configurations

articles.title: Home Assistant sets Nintendo play restrictions in advance
articles.dek: Parents can change a chosen day’s limits without waiting for that day to arrive.
body: Home Assistant adds an action for updating Nintendo Parental Controls restrictions on a specific day. The existing controls change whichever day is current, which meant parents had to wait until the intended day to adjust it.
Jordan Harvey adds the targeted action and its guide, giving household automations a way to prepare a particular day’s restrictions in advance.

pullRequests.title: Add service to update individual day restrictions in Nintendo Parental Controls
Add documentation for updating daily restrictions

articles.title: Music Assistant’s mobile playlists include radio and audiobooks
articles.dek: Mixed playlists keep their original order and become available through CarPlay.
body: Music Assistant’s mobile app stops dropping radio stations and audiobooks from playlists. Mixed lists retain their original order, and CarPlay’s playlist browser includes the same items instead of keeping only music tracks.

Andrii Mitnovych also adds playlist actions to podcast episode pages. The add-to-playlist chooser hides service playlists that cannot accept the selected kind of item, avoiding a request that the server would silently discard.
